text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- A wide range of commemorations marked the 40th anniversary of the Hungarian Revolution and the 7th anniversary of the proclamation of the republic on Wednesday. @

- Arpad Kovacs, nominee for the post of chairman of the board of the State Privatisation and Holding Co. (APV) said that privatisation will be suspended for a temporary period since the new board will have to review all cases left pending.
- Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy said Tuesday a further drop in real wages and domestic consumption can be avoided without jeopardising economic equilibrium.

- NATO European forces commander-in-chief Gen. George Joulwan announced in Budapest Tuesday that Hungarian officers would be given positions in the multinational command to be set up for IFOR forces monitoring peace in Bosnia. @

- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs said yesterday that the Hungarian cabinet welcomes the speech delivered by US President Bill Clinton in which he said the first group of East European countries applying for NATO membership must become full members by 1999.
- The deficit of the balance of payments came to $99 million in August, reports the National Bank of Hungary.
- The US credit-rating institute Moody's may improve the rating of five Hungarian commercial banks, Moody's leaders announced Tuesday.
VILAGGAZDASAG @
- This paper reports that an investigation by the Supervisory Board of APV will blame former APV chiefs for the land deals concluded with local governments.

- The cabinet is due to take a close look at tasks resulting from an investigation into the credit, banking and debt consolidation scheme, and hear a report on the repayment by Russia of its state debt at its meeting today.
- The chemical giant BorsodChem has completed a HUF 3 billion capacity increase.
- The state may sell some or all of its shares in Richter and MOL in the first six months of 1997. @
- An independent organisation will be set up today to provide credit information on Hungarian companies, said Pal Kapitany, director of the Credit Protection Union.
MAGYAR NEMZET
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn and Austrian Chancellor Franz Vranitzky will today attend the formal inauguration of the Hungarian-Austrian Gyor-Baumgarten gas pipeline.
- Foreign ministers of Italy, Slovenia and Hungary signed an agreement in Rome yesterday on forging closer ties in the economic, political, military, security and cultural fields.
NEPSZABADSAG @

- Privatisation in Hungary should not come to a halt because of the recent scandals, as the country's EU membership depends on the maturity of the private sector, argued Michel Noel, head of the World Bank's Central European division.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- The US-based Cuna Mutual Group plans to participate in the privatisation of Takarekbank, the bank of savings cooperatives, said vice president Jacek C. Clanciara.
- The exchange of shares in the southwest Hungarian gas distribution company Dedasz for compensation coupons closes today. @

- Analysts of Creditanstalt Securities suggest that owners of shares in Horizon-Multiplan, a small Hungarian company producing a nutritional supplement, should sell their securities. -- Budapest newsroom (36-1) 327 4040
